_: The variant register. This file is the source of truth for index.html — the
portal that sits beside the variants — for `npm run shoot`, and for the BUILD:
vite.config.js reads it to decide what to compile, so a version is added in
exactly ONE place.
A VARIANT IS A FILE, NOT A BRANCH AND NOT A FOLDER. `file` is both the source
name under src/ and the published name at the top of this folder — Vite's root
is src/ and it names an output HTML file by its path relative to root, so the
two agree with no renaming step to get wrong. Assets for every version land in
one hashed assets1/, because they are built in a single pass and share three.js,
the decoders and the model rather than carrying a copy each.
Order is presentation order: newest first. `status` is free text and appears
on the card as written — 'current', 'superseded', 'experiment', a date, or
nothing at all.
A VARIANT IS A PAGE; A DIRECTION IS AN ART DIRECTION. indexA/B/C.html are the
three directions explored off index1. They share one bootstrap (src/site/vboot.js)
and differ in src/directions/{a,b,c}.js and site/dir-{a,b,c}.css. An entry with a
`direction` key is GENERATED by tools/gen-variants.mjs, which publish.mjs runs
before every build — the letter is the name end to end, so there is no mapping
between the direction you are editing and the page you are opening. index1.html
has no `direction` and is hand-authored.
A variant is REMOVED by deleting its entry here, deleting its index<name>.html
A VARIANT MAY ALSO PUBLISH UNDER ALIASES. `alias` is a list of extra names the
built page is copied to at the top of this folder. It exists because index1.html
is the CANONICAL URL for this folder — it is the name the dashboard links, the
name every other _buro test uses, and the one Alex hands out — while the page
that URL should serve changes as the work moves on. An alias keeps the URL and
the source decoupled: tools/publish.mjs copies dist/<file> to <file> and then to
every alias, so the mapping is reproduced by `npm run publish` from a clean
checkout and cannot drift into a hand-copied file nobody can regenerate.
Two entries may not claim the same published name; publish.mjs refuses the run
rather than letting copy order decide which page wins the URL.

title: Machine study 01
subject: KUKA KR 700 PA

variants.name: Presentation
variants.note: The company around the machine. Nine chapters over one unbroken 478° camera take, with the stage changing register chapter by chapter — full, veiled, render window, macro, a film plate laid over the frame before it, quiet, held — and a last screen that stops in true profile and can be turned. Five callouts set as single annotation lines. Desktop only. Published as the canonical index1.html for this folder as well as under its own name.

variants.name: Monumental
variants.note: Direction A. The machine as architecture — cropped on two or three edges in every shot, one hard source and almost no fill, and ten numbered callouts carrying the language in place of shot statements.

variants.name: Editorial
variants.note: Direction B. The type IS the composition: the designation and the figures set at 19–34vw and cropped by the viewport, with the machine passing in front of some words and behind others. Nine callouts, set into the type grid.

variants.name: Machine film
variants.note: Direction C. Shot as a film about a machine: a cold open on one joint, light that warms through the middle and resolves cool, one line of copy per beat and six callouts in the whole run.

variants.name: The level line
variants.note: Six camera stations around roughly 490° of travel. The datum lives in the room rather than on the glass, so the arm occludes it. Split-flap opening; instrument layer reads real azimuth and distance.
